writeup: TIC 224306120 is a candidate eclipsing binary star identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 1.23 percent and an orbital period of 4.1752 days, producing a strong detection signal with a BLS signal-to-noise ratio of 81.0. No secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level image analysis yielded a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 5.5, though the centroid offset of 13.7 arcsec from the target warrants consideration. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel identification. The machine-learning screening assigned it a score of 0.84, indicating high likelihood of being a genuine eclipsing system, and the data passed all quality checks without flags.
